text:
Nina (SRE): Postmortem follow-up: the private tenant experienced repeated control-plane timeouts when VPC peering flapped. Root hints point to MTU blackholes + asymmetric return routing. We need: named owners, short ETA, and an oncall-friendly checklist.

Gina (Eng-Infra): I'll take ownership of the validation checks and runbook fragments. Plan: create a `peering-health` probe that runs MTU and reassembly checks and posts to infra metrics. ETA: 3 business days.

Omar (Private Deploy): I'll implement an agent-side workaround (MSS clamping + conservative 3-way handshake retries) as opt-in config. Will prepare a canary plan for staging. ETA: end of sprint unless customer logs show clear pattern (then I'll fast-track).

Ben (Support): Logged with affected customer; they've agreed to run `tcpdump` during the next window and share pcap. I created ticket INC-5024 and added our engineers.

Nina (SRE): Minimal oncall checklist to add to runbook:
- run `ping -M do -s <size>` to probe PMTU
- `traceroute --mtu` (if available) to spot path drops
- check peering status via cloud API and BGP tables
- when to escalate to Dedicated fallback (criteria + owner contact)

Gina (Eng-Infra): Example quick commands for runbook:
```bash
# PMTU probe
ping -M do -s 1400 -c 3 10.2.3.4
# detect fragments seen on host
sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 'ip[6:2] & 0x3fff != 0' -c 50
# cloud peering state
az network vnet peering show --name peername --resource-group rg
``` 
I'll put the probe in infra-monitoring so it can run per-region on a schedule.

Omar (Private Deploy): Implementation notes: some customer firewalls drop fragments silently. We'll add an `agent.mss_clamp` boolean with default false; ops can flip it during incident for affected tenants. Canary will mirror small percent of traffic.

ticket-bot: INC-5024 created and assigned to: Ben, Gina, Omar. Priority: P2.

Ben (Support): Uploaded first pcap to INC-5024. I see repeated ICMP fragmentation-needed messages and out-of-order ACKs.

Nina (SRE): Action items recap and owners:
- Gina: peering-health probe + runbook snippet (ETA 3 business days)
- Omar: agent opt-in MSS clamp + canary plan (ETA end of sprint / expedite if pcaps confirm)
- Ben: collect additional pcaps and device configs (ETA tomorrow)
- Nina: add escalation matrix and dedicated fallback procedure to runbook (ETA Fri)

Gina (Eng-Infra): Quick question: prefer runbook in `private-deploy/runbooks` or `infra/runbooks`? I vote infra so scheduled probes and alerts are co-located.

Omar (Private Deploy): Agree infra-runbooks for probes. But please add link to private-deploy onboarding to explain opt-in agent flag.

Ben (Support): Noted overlap: INC-4888 had similar symptoms last quarter. I'll link and tag as recurring class "vpc-peering-mtu".

Nina (SRE): Good. We'll keep this as the canonical thread and update INC-5024 as the single source of truth. If INC-5024 is still open after one week we'll move to a recurring 15m sync to track reduction in affected tenants.

Gina (Eng-Infra): :thumbsup:

Omar (Private Deploy): :thumbsup:

Ben (Support): :thumbsup:
